pages.text: I built my first rocket at a bench that drank plutonium, and fuelled it with oil from the deep wells. I sealed myself into a suit, checked the air twice, and pressed the button.
The Moon was silent. Mars was red and hungry. Venus burned and rained acid; Mercury hugged the sun. And around another star entirely: Glacio, frozen, the most beautiful place I ever stood.
Each world had a guardian, stronger than anything at home. From each I took a sigil, and from each sigil and that world's metal I forged a core. Five worlds, held in my hands.
I built a home out there, with air and water and one crop growing in alien soil. Then I gathered a piece of every age I had lived through and bound them around a star.
This is where my chronicle should end. The Emblem, the five cores and a drop of antimatter forge the Heart of the Ages. I never did. My hands shook too much. The last page is blank. It is yours.
A table, bronze, a key, a core, a mechanism, a capacitor, a pellet and a helmet. Everything you built led here.
pages.title: Mark of the Space Age
